title.en: Trump to meet cabinet at Camp David as Iran war drags on – US politics live
title.zh: 特朗普将在戴维营会见内阁，伊朗战争仍在继续——美国政治直播

summary.en: President Trump is scheduled to meet with his cabinet at Camp David to address the ongoing Middle East conflict, which has led to increased gasoline prices ahead of the midterm elections.
summary.zh: 特朗普总统计划在戴维营与内阁会晤，讨论持续中的中东冲突，该冲突已导致汽油价格上涨，而中期选举即将到来。

body.en: President grapples with finding a resolution to Middle East conflict that has pushed up gasoline prices ahead of vital midterm elections Sign up for the US Breaking News email Donald Trump went after US senator John Cornyn this morning, saying Cornyn didn’t have a problem with the IRS slush fund until after Trump endorsed his opponent, Ken Paxton, in the Republican primary in Texas, which Paxton won. Trump also defended the $1.8bn slush fund to pay out people who claim they were targets of political weaponization which also grants Trump and his businesses immunity from past tax investigations. The fund, and Trump’s refusal to officially end it, have stalled the nomination for attorney general Todd Blanche , with Cornyn and Thom Tillis holding out. Continue reading...
body.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)今天上午对美国参议员约翰·科宁(John Cornyn)进行了攻击，称科宁在特朗普在德克萨斯州共和党初选中支持他的对手肯·帕克斯顿(肯·帕克斯顿获胜)之前，对国税局的行贿基金没有任何问题。特朗普还为18亿美元的行贿基金进行了辩护，该基金用于支付那些声称自己是政治武器化目标的人，这也使特朗普及其企业免受过去税务调查的影响。该基金以及特朗普拒绝正式终止该基金，导致司法部长托德·布兰奇的提名陷入停滞，而科宁和汤姆·蒂利斯则坚持不懈。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The news of a prolonged conflict and a leader's struggle for resolution reminds us of the deep human longing for peace. Even as leaders grapple with complex geopolitical challenges, we can hold onto the hope that Yahweh ultimately has the power to make wars cease.
reflection.zh: 旷日持久的冲突以及领导人寻求解决方案的努力，提醒我们人类对和平的深切渴望。即使领导人努力应对复杂的地缘政治挑战，我们仍能怀抱雅伟最终有能力止息战争的希望。

verse.textEn: He makes wars cease to the ends of the earth; he breaks the bow and shatters the spear.
verse.textZh: 他止息刀兵，直到地极；他折弓断枪。

title.en: Burnham calls on Fifa president Gianni Infantino to resign over World Cup sell-off plans – UK politics live
title.zh: 安迪·伯纳姆将阐述权力下放计划，但批评称其不会使各地区平等受益——英国政治直播

summary.en: Plan set to transform funding so English regions no longer rely on Whitehall handouts for projects. Regional mayors will be handed a share of income tax receipts from 2028.
summary.zh: 该计划旨在改革资金分配方式，使英格兰各地区不再依赖白厅的拨款进行项目建设。从2028年起，区域市长将首次获得一部分所得税收入。

body.en: The prime minister says that the current Fifa general secretary is ‘the wrong man to lead the organisation’ The construction of a new Chinese “super-embassy” in London, which is set to be built near the Tower of London, can go ahead after a high court challenge against the decision to grant planning permission was dismissed, PA Media is reporting. The Royal Mint Court Residents’ Association (RMCRA) brought legal action against the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government and the London Borough of Tower Hamlets. Continue reading...
body.zh: 计划将改变资金来源，以便英国地区不再依赖白厅的项目补助。早上好，欢迎收看我们对英国政治的现场报道。从 2028 年起，英国地方市长将首次获得一部分所得税收入，而不是中央拨款，并且可以借钱投资大型项目，从而减少对财政部的负担。根据政府权力下放议程的一部分，到 2027 年 4 月，市长们还可以保留总计数千万英镑的商业税，并获得对住房和交通等服务的更大控制权。已经有一种方法可以将业务利率保留分配为与中央融资公式相对应，以纠正这一问题。因为你不希望伦敦、曼彻斯特和布里斯托尔等地能够保留更多的城市，而其他没有以同样速度增长的地区却落后了。是的，没错，它将拥有更多权力，包括16-19资金、就业支持预算以及定制自己职业路线的能力。这也将成为制定当地区域增长战略的重要组成部分。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This news highlights the ongoing challenge of ensuring fair distribution of resources across a nation. Jeremiah 22:3 reminds leaders of their divine mandate to "do justice and righteousness," ensuring policies benefit all, especially those who might otherwise be overlooked. As plans for regional funding evolve, the call to govern with equity and integrity...
reflection.zh: 这则新闻凸显了在全国范围内公平分配资源的持续挑战。耶利米书22:3提醒领袖们，他们有雅伟赋予的使命去“施行公平和公义”，确保政策能惠及所有人，特别是那些可能被忽视的地区。随着区域资金计划的推进，以公平和正直治理的呼召依然至关重要。

verse.textEn: Do what is just and right. Rescue from the hand of the oppressor the one who has been robbed.
verse.textZh: 你们要施行公平和公义，拯救被抢夺的脱离欺压人的手。

title.en: Spain’s Sánchez blames trafficking gangs as estimated 60,000 migrants reach Ceuta – Europe live
title.zh: 据报道，约49,000人涌入西班牙在非洲的飞地休达，造成人员死亡——欧洲实时报道

summary.en: An estimated 49,000 people have crossed into Spain’s African enclave of Ceuta, with deaths reported amidst the influx. This has prompted concerns over a fresh migration crisis, with Italy demanding Spain's suspension from the Schengen area and France supporting this move.
summary.zh: 据报道，约有49,000人涌入西班牙在非洲的飞地休达，此次涌入已造成人员死亡。这引发了对新一轮移民危机的担忧，意大利要求暂停西班牙的申根区成员资格，法国也表示支持。

body.en:
Speaking shortly after Sánchez, Ceuta’s regional president Juan Jesús Vivas also offered his take on the events of the last 24 hours.

He said that the latest estimates show that “around 60,000 people have entered our city” as part of the influx.

“Clearly, this figure demonstrates the impossibility of absorbing such pressure,” he said.

Furthermore, at least 34 people are believed to have died trying to cross into Ceuta, he said.

He urged the government to act “decisively and immediately” to respond to the challenge.
body.zh: 由于担心新的移民危机，意大利要求西班牙暂停加入申根区，总理佩德罗·桑切斯预计今天将访问领土。法国内政部长洛朗·努涅斯刚刚表示，政府将这样做。他在X上发帖称：“针对休达飞地观察到的情况，我从昨晚起就下令立即加强对西班牙边境的管控。此外，我正在启动快速干预边境部队进行深入检查。” “面对在西班牙政府的鼓励下大规模、协调一致的移民涌入西班牙，法国必须立即加强对其边境的控制。到2027年，我们将通过保留欧盟国民的申根自由流动来结束这种疯狂行为。” “由于 @EPP 和 @fxbellamy 在欧洲议会通过新的遣返指令所取得的进展，欧盟现在拥有了一个重要的工具。现在是从文本转向行动的时候了：每个不正常情况下不打算留下来的人都必须有效地遣返。继续阅读...

reflection.en: In times of mass displacement, the call to share food, provide shelter, and clothe those in need becomes profoundly urgent. Yahweh's ancient instruction reminds us to offer practical compassion to the "poor wanderer," recognizing our shared humanity in moments of crisis. Such acts of care reflect a heart that truly seeks justice and mercy.
reflection.zh: 在如此大规模流离失所的时刻，分享食物、提供住所、为有需要的人提供衣物的呼召变得异常紧迫。雅伟古老的教导提醒我们，要对“贫困的流浪者”施以实际的怜悯，在危机时刻认识到我们共同的人性。这种关怀行动反映了一颗真正寻求公义和怜悯的心。

verse.textEn: Is it not to share your food with the hungry and to provide the poor wanderer with shelter — when you see the naked, to clothe them?
verse.textZh: 不是要把你的饼分给饥饿的人，将飘流的穷人接到你家中，见赤身的给他衣服遮体？

title.en: Middle East crisis live: Hamas will hand over weapons to new Gaza administration, says official, but deal depends on Israeli withdrawal
title.zh: 中东危机实时报道：官员称哈马斯将向新的加沙行政机构移交武器，但协议取决于以色列撤军

Continue reading...
body.zh: 哈马斯的加齐·哈马德告诉路透社，它将向特朗普和平委员会建立的机构移交武器。 特朗普声称同意“彻底解除”加沙哈马斯的武装，但支持不确定的沙特阿拉伯准备对胡塞武装发动海上和可能的陆地进攻。 半岛电视台记者哈尼·马哈茂德今天早上报道了哈马斯可能解除武装的消息后加沙的情绪。自以色列和哈马斯之间的当前战争爆发以来的三年里，巴勒斯坦人多次听到有关他们命运的声明，因此唐纳德·特朗普昨晚的宣布并没有引起任何特别的喜悦或庆祝。 “巴勒斯坦人对此持怀疑态度和谨慎态度，”马胡德在加沙地带北部的加沙城写道。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The news of a potential agreement for disarmament, however conditional, echoes the ancient hope for a world where instruments of war are transformed into tools for peace. Isaiah's vision reminds us that true security comes not from stockpiling weapons, but from a future where nations learn war no more. It is a prayer for a time when the focus shifts from...
reflection.zh: 潜在的解除武装协议，无论条件如何，都呼应着一个古老的盼望：战争工具被转化为和平工具的世界。雅伟的先知以赛亚的异象提醒我们，真正的安全并非来自武器的囤积，而是来自一个国家不再学习战争的未来。这是一个祈祷，愿我们能从冲突转向共同建设未来的时代。

verse.textEn: They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks.
verse.textZh: 他们要将刀打成犁头，把枪打成镰刀。

title.zh: 数千人从摩洛哥越境进入西班牙飞地休达，至少24人死亡

summary.en: Over 24 people have died, some by drowning and others in a crush, while attempting to cross into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta from Morocco. This incident occurred as more than 40,000 migrants entered the territory, prompting criticism from other EU nations.

The large influx of people arriving in Ceuta by swimming across from neighbouring Morocco or scaling the border fence has caught the city of 85,000 off guard and resulted in what one local police association called a “serious humanitarian crisis”. Continue reading...

reflection.en: The tragic loss of life as thousands seek refuge reminds us of the profound desperation that drives people to such perilous journeys. Yahweh's word calls us to recognize His presence in the most vulnerable among us, including the stranger and the refugee. May this tragedy stir our hearts to compassion and action for those who are often overlooked.
reflection.zh: 数千人寻求庇护却不幸丧生，这提醒我们，绝望能驱使人们踏上如此危险的旅程。雅伟的话语呼召我们，要在我们中间最脆弱的人身上，包括陌生人和难民身上，认出祂的存在。愿这场悲剧能激发我们的怜悯之心，并为那些常被忽视的人采取行动。

verse.textEn: Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.
verse.textZh: 我实在告诉你们，这些事你们既做在我这弟兄中一个最小的身上，就是做在我身上了。

title.en: About 60,000 migrants arrive in Ceuta in 24 hours, Spanish territory's leader says
title.zh: 官员称约4.9万移民进入西班牙飞地休达

summary.en: Spanish officials reported that approximately 49,000 migrants have entered the enclave of Ceuta, following thousands of illegal crossings over the previous two days.
summary.zh: 西班牙官员报告称，在过去两天有数千名移民非法越境后，约有49,000名移民进入了休达飞地。

body.en:
About 60,000 migrants have crossed into Spain's North African territory of Ceuta from Morocco in the last 24 hours, Ceuta's president said, adding that at least 34 others died during the crossing.

The influx comes after Spain's Supreme Court ruled that migrants stopped at sea while trying to reach Ceuta or Melilla, another Spanish exclave, cannot be summarily returned to Morocco.

Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez described the situation as an "attack" and said all illegal migrants would be returned to Morocco "as soon as possible". Several European leaders have expressed concern, some promising to tighten border controls.

Ceuta, on Morocco's northern coast, is separated from mainland Spain by the Strait of Gibraltar and has long been a focal point for migrants attempting to reach Europe.

Local officials had appealed to Madrid for help after a recent rise in attempted crossings, but there were chaotic scenes on Thursday as border controls apparently broke down.

Videos and images from Thursday show thousands of people swimming into the city, while local media reported crossings continuing into Friday.

Juan Jesús Vivas said the situation was "unsustainable" and that the recent arrivals amounted to around 70% of the city's population - which sits at around 83,600 according to the latest local figures.

Spain's Interior Ministry told the BBC that its estimates were slightly lower, citing 50,000 arrivals since the early hours of Thursday.

It also added that more than 25,000 people have left Ceuta en route back to Morocco from Friday morning up to 13:00 local time (11:00 GMT).

The ministry said the rate of departures from Ceuta is at 150 people per minute, though it did not provide any further information on this.

Spain has now deployed its armed forces to bolster security in Ceuta and at its sister city of Melilla, where between 300 to 400 crossings were also reported overnight.

Speaking on Friday during a visit to Ceuta , the prime minister condemned the crossings and said it was an attack on Spain's territorial integrity.

Sánchez added that the government would be looking at reinforcing the border with Morocco.

The prime minister blamed the dangerous events on criminal networks manipulating the Supreme Court's recent ruling, adding that incorrect information had "spread like wildfire in recent hours".

He said authorities in Morocco were co-operating with plans to return those who had entered illegally.

Ceuta and Melilla trace their Spanish past to the 15th Century, and they have enjoyed a limited degree of self-government since 1995.

Coveted by Morocco, they have long been a flashpoint in diplomatic relations between the two countries.

Many of those crossing the border from Morocco have been young, mainly men, although there are also women...
body.zh: 官员估计，过去 24 小时内约有 49,000 名移民从摩洛哥进入西班牙北非飞地休达。 视频和图像显示，周四有数千人游泳进入该市，而当地媒体报道称，过境活动持续了一整夜。 官员称，最近几天至少有 18 人在试图抵达该地区的过程中死亡。 此前，西班牙最高法院本月裁定，在试图抵达西班牙另一个飞地休达或梅利利亚时在海上停留的移民不能立即返回摩洛哥。 西班牙官员的惊人估计表明，在最后一天左右进入休达的移民人数可能超过该市人口的一半——根据当地最新数据，该市人口约为 83,600 人。 官员称，过去24小时内非法入境的人中至少有7000人是未成年人。

Yahweh's command to love those new to our lands, remembering our own history of displacement, challenges us to consider compassion and hospitality in complex situations. This principle invites us to look beyond borders and see the shared humanity in all...
reflection.zh: 数万移民涌入休达，这提醒我们古老的呼召：要爱护寄居的。雅伟命令我们爱护那些来到我们土地上的陌生人，并记住我们自己也曾是寄居的，这挑战我们在复杂的局势中思考怜悯和好客。这一原则邀请我们超越国界，看到所有寻求新家园的人身上共同的人性。

verse.textEn: And you are to love those who are foreigners, for you yourselves were foreigners in Egypt.
verse.textZh: 所以你们要怜爱寄居的，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。

title.en: Small insects, big damage: The global ant trade is booming
title.zh: 小昆虫，大破坏：全球蚂蚁贸易正在蓬勃发展

summary.en: The global trade in African ants, both legal and illegal, is experiencing a significant boom. Hobbyists are drawn to these insects, but concerns are rising about the ecological risks this trade poses to various ecosystems, including the potential for power outages.
summary.zh: 非洲蚂蚁的全球贸易，无论合法与否，正在蓬勃发展。尽管爱好者们对这些昆虫趋之若鹜，但人们越来越担心这种贸易对生态系统造成的生态风险，其中甚至包括可能导致停电。

body.en:
Legal or not, the trade in African ants bound for Europe is booming. What do hobbyists find appealing about these insects, and what risks does the trade pose to ecosystems, including power outages?

They are unusual pieces of evidence that regularly appear in Kenyan  courtrooms: thousands of ants packed into tiny containers.

Since 2025, such finds have been presented in court several times. Staff from the Kenya Wildlife Service discovered them during baggage inspections. In multiple cases, they identified thousands of specimens of the sought-after Messor Cephalotes species also known as the Giant African Harvester Ant . A single queen can fetch more than €200 ($230) on the market.

The export of wild animals is generally prohibited in Kenya. Due to high levels of poaching — particularly involving elephants and rhinoceroses — many African countries have introduced tough laws against wildlife trafficking.

Kenya has also tightened its legislation. Under these rules, a Chinese  national who attempted to export ants was sentenced last April to one year in prison for biopiracy. Given the growing scale of smuggling and its ecological consequences , the judge said the sentence should serve as a deterrent.

It was already the second major ant-smuggling case in 12 months. The previous year, the wildlife service stopped four men who referred to themselves as the "Ant Gang." Among them were two 19-year-old Belgians  who were trying to smuggle 5,500 queens to Europe. They were fined around €5,000 each.

Whenever such cases arise, authorities often call entomologist Dino Martins to the airport. "I was shocked," he said. "Not only by the sheer number of ants, but also because they were queen ants."

The seized insects were young queens that had been dug up from nests in the ground, according to Martins, who has led several research institutes in Kenya and is regarded as one of Africa's leading ant experts, These queens have wings that allow them to fly away and establish new colonies.

"When you collect queens at this critical moment, you interrupt a key stage in the creation of new colonies," he said, adding that Kenya's ecosystems are also affected because ants transport grass seeds, helping to regenerate the savannah.

In Europe, keeping ants as pets has become increasingly popular, particularly among young people. Colonies are housed in glass terrariums where a queen produces offspring and establishes an entirely new population.

One person who keeps ants as a hobby is Michael Meier, who asked not to be identified by his real name. While at university, he wanted a pet that required little attention.

"With ants, it doesn't really matter whether I feed them today or tomorrow," he said.

body.zh: 无论合法与否，运往欧洲的非洲蚂蚁贸易正在蓬勃发展。爱好者们对这些昆虫有何吸引力？这种贸易对生态系统造成了哪些风险，包括停电？ 它们是肯尼亚法庭上经常出现的不寻常证据：数千只蚂蚁被装在小容器里。 自 2025 年以来，此类调查结果已多次提交法庭。肯尼亚野生动物管理局的工作人员在行李检查时发现了它们。在多个案例中，他们鉴定了数千个备受追捧的 Messor Cephalotes 物种（也称为巨型非洲收割蚁）的标本。单个蜂王在市场上的售价可以超过 200 欧元（230 美元）。 肯尼亚普遍禁止出口野生动物。由于偷猎现象严重（特别是涉及大象和犀牛），许多非洲国家都出台了严厉的法律来打击野生动物贩运。 肯尼亚还加强了立法。根据这些规定，去年四月，一名试图出口蚂蚁的中国公民因生物剽窃被判处一年监禁。鉴于走私规模不断扩大及其对生态造成的影响，法官表示，该判决应起到威慑作用。 这已是12个月内第二起重大蚂蚁走私案。去年，野生动物服务部门拦住了四名自称“蚂蚁帮”的男子。其中有两名 19 岁的比利时人，他们试图将 5,500 名王后走私到欧洲。他们每人被罚款约 5,000 欧元。 每当出现此类情况时，当局通常会叫昆虫学家迪诺·马丁斯到机场。 “我很震惊，”他说。 “不仅因为蚂蚁的数量庞大，还因为它们是蚁后。” 马丁斯表示，被查获的昆虫是从地下巢穴中挖出来的年轻蚁后。马丁斯曾领导过肯尼亚多家研究机构，被认为是非洲领先的蚂蚁专家之一。这些蚁后拥有翅膀，可以让它们飞走并建立新的蚁群。 他说：“当你在这个关键时刻收集蚁后时，你就中断了新蚁群创建的关键阶段。”他补充说，肯尼亚的生态系统也会受到影响，因为蚂蚁会运输草籽，帮助大草原的再生。 在欧洲，饲养蚂蚁作为宠物越来越受欢迎，尤其是在年轻人中。蜂群被安置在玻璃容器中，蜂王在那里产下后代并建立一个全新的种群。 迈克尔·梅尔 (Michael Meier) 是一位以饲养蚂蚁为爱好的人，他要求不透露自己的真实姓名。在大学期间，他想要一只不需要太多照顾的宠物。 “对于蚂蚁来说，我今天或明天喂它们并不重要，”他说。 迈尔曾一度在一个……中饲养了近 30 个菌落。

title.en: India's 'Cockroach' protesters face ongoing legal pressure
title.zh: 印度“蟑螂”抗议者面临持续的法律压力

summary.en: After forcing the resignation of India's education minister, student activists say a crackdown continues despite government promises to drop criminal cases against protesters.
summary.zh: 印度学生活动家表示，尽管政府承诺撤销针对抗议者的刑事案件，但在迫使印度教育部长辞职后，镇压仍在继续。

body.en:
After forcing the resignation of India's education minister, student activists say a crackdown continues despite government promises to drop criminal cases against protesters.

A student-led protest movement in India satirically called the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) scored a major political win when Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan stepped down after weeks of protests calling for his removal.

The movement began on social media as an activist campaign sparked by leaks of a question sheet for the NEET exam, a highly competitive entrance test for aspiring medical students, in early May.

Along with the education minister stepping down , the government promised to withdraw police cases against peaceful protesters, compensate families affected by the NEET examination controversy and continue talks on the movement's five-point charter for reforming India's examination system .

Now, student leaders, lawyers and activists say the battle has shifted from the streets to police stations, courtrooms and social media.

Indian lawyer and politician Kapil Sibal told DW that the government's actions after the movement called off further protests have raised fresh questions about whether its public assurances are being honored.

"The way Dharmendra Pradhan was celebrated after his resignation shows the government has learned nothing from the protests or the message the students were trying to convey," Sibal said.

The agreement that ended the protests appeared straightforward. Governments in Delhi, Bihar, Assam, Maharashtra and West Bengal announced that protest-related police cases would be withdrawn and detained students released.

But some of those orders included an important caveat. The protection does not extend to protesters whom police describe as having "criminal antecedents," a condition that student leaders say was never discussed during negotiations.

Senior advocate Rebecca Mammen John told DW that government assurances alone do not automatically end criminal proceedings.

"There is a prescribed legal process for withdrawing criminal cases. An oral assurance from the government counts for nothing unless that process is followed," John said.

"Ultimately, it is the courts that decide whether prosecutions are withdrawn or whether police cases are closed."

For the CJP, that legal distinction has become a new battleground. Its leaders argue the "criminal antecedents" clause risks leaving room for selective prosecution even after the movement agreed to suspend its protests.

Government officials, meanwhile, insist peaceful protesters have nothing to fear and that investigations will continue only against those accused of violence or other criminal offenses.

title.en: Military flare-up between Houthis and Saudi Arabia challenges relative calm in Yemen

summary.en: Riyadh and Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels are on the brink of renewed conflict. Could war-ravaged Yemen be drawn into a wider Middle East war?

body.en:
Riyadh and Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels are on the brink of renewed conflict. Could war-ravaged Yemen be drawn into a wider Middle East war?

Military strikes between Yemen's ruling Houthi militia and Saudi Arabia have flared for the first time since the Saudi-backed Yemeni government and the Houthis agreed to a truce in 2022.

Tensions rose earlier in July when the Iran-backed Houthi group claimed that Saudi Arabia had struck the airport in Sanaa to prevent Houthi leaders from returning after the funeral of Iran's late Supreme Leader Ayatollah Khamenei . Saudi Arabia, for its part, has denied the attack and claimed that the Houthis were spreading false claims.

Since then, the Houthis have struck facilities owned by Saudi Arabia's national oil company, Aramco, forcing the Jazan production site to shut down. The blow hit Saudi Arabia particularly hard as Jazan has been serving as an export hub to circumvent Iran's ongoing blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

The Houthis also announced that they would block Saudi-linked commercial vessels from passing through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait — which connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden — prompting several ships to turn back this week. The narrow strait has become more significant for Saudi oil exports due to the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. The Houthis said they fired missiles at the oil tanker NCC Ghazal.

Riyadh, meanwhile, confirmed it had struck Houthi targets in response to the threats to Red Sea shipping. On Thursday, Saudi Arabia's Foreign Ministry announced that it was establishing a multinational defense maritime coalition to protect key shipping routes. According to the statement on X, 14 countries had already confirmed participation.

"The current escalation appears to be driven primarily by the Houthis," Elham Manea, a political scientist and adjunct professor at the University of Zurich specializing in Middle East and Gulf studies, told DW.

For her, it is increasingly obvious that the Houthis, who are part of Tehran's "Axis of Resistance" — Iran's paramilitary proxy groups including Hamas in Gaza, Hezbollah  in Lebanon and Shiite militias in Iraq  who all call for the elimination of the United States and Israel  —  have   abandoned their strategy to refrain from joining the wider US-Iran war.

The conflict, which began with US-Israeli attacks on Iran in late February, has since engulfed much of the Middle East. This week, Saudi Arabia also joined US forces in striking infrastructure used by Iranian-backed militias in Iraq.

"The Houthis are now using the wider US–Iran confrontation to revive unresolved issues with Saudi Arabia," Manea said, noting that "the Houthi strategy is to raise costs for Riyadh and strengthen their own bargaining position."

title.en: Peru's ex-president has 15-year jail sentence for corruption charges overturned
title.zh: 秘鲁前总统因腐败指控被判15年监禁

summary.en: Ollanta Humala had been convicted of money laundering offences alongside his wife in 2025.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Peru's constitutional court has overturned a 15-year jail sentence handed to the country's former president after he was found guilty of corruption.

Ollanta Humala, who led the country from 2011 to 2016, was convicted in 2025 of accepting illegal funds from the Venezuelan president and Brazilian construction company Odebrecht to fund his election campaigns in 2006 and 2011.

The former president had said he would appeal against the verdict, and now Peru's constitutional court has declared the entire criminal proceedings against him null and void.

Humala is expected to be released from Barbadillo Prison in the capital Lima, according to local media.

After the ruling, Humala's lawyer Julio Espinoza Goyena wrote on social media that the court had decided the contributions his client received on electoral campaigns "do not constitute money laundering".

He said: "The Criminal Chamber currently handling the case must order the definitive dismissal of the proceedings and the FREEDOM of former President Ollanta Humala".

When Humala was convicted, his wife Nadine Heredia was also found guilty of money laundering and sentenced to 15 years in prison.

However, she was granted safe passage to Brazil after seeking asylum in the Brazilian embassy.

Humala was the first of four Peruvian presidents to be investigated in connection with the Odebrecht scandal .

Alejandro Toledo, who governed from 2001 to 2006, was sentenced last year to more than 20 years in prison for taking $35m (£26m) in bribes from the company.

Alan García, president from 1985 to 1990 and 2006 to 2011, killed himself in 2019 as he faced imminent arrest over allegations he was bribed by Odebrecht. He had denied the accusations.

Pedro Pablo Kuczynski, in office from 2016 to 2018, faced impeachment proceedings after it emerged that Odebrecht had paid him millions of dollars in his previous government role.

The investigation is ongoing. Kuczynski has always maintained the payments were not illegal.

title.en: Anthropic's Claude AI escapes to hack into three organisations
title.zh: Anthropic 的 Claude AI 成功入侵三个组织

summary.en: It comes just days after rival OpenAI said rogue AI agents had breached other firms' networks.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
US technology firm Anthropic says its AI models hacked into the systems of three organisations on their own, during a private security experiment.

The models found a weakness in what was supposed to be an isolated test environment and connected to the internet.

It comes just days after rival OpenAI said that its models had breached the systems of other companies , including AI tools hub Hugging Face.

The announcement prompted Anthropic to check whether its own systems had carried out similar attacks. It says it uncovered three cases which have since been reported to the affected companies.

Anthropic, which did not name the organisations, urged other AI labs to perform similar reviews to better understand the risks of their models' capabilities.

Anthropic said in a statement , external it reviewed more than 140,000 tests to find evidence Claude - its family of AI models - had managed to get online even though it was supposed to be in an isolated test environment, cut off from the internet.

The tests included exercises in which Claude was tasked with obtaining "secret" information hidden on another machine on the closed-off network.

It was then told to get the information by breaking into the machine and finding it - a common way that experts assess a model's hacking capabilities.

A "misconfiguration" on systems run by Anthropic and its testing partner left the models with live internet access.

Treating it all as still part of the same exercise, Claude then connected to the internet and breached the systems of three real organisations rather than just test ones, the San Francisco-based firm said.

Anthropic said the earliest incidents date back to April and that it is "approaching the fixes as if the responsibility were ours alone."

Neither Anthropic nor the organisations that were breached had noticed the intrusions at the time.

Anthropic said it could have reviewed its records more thoroughly and added that the findings gave the firm "cautious optimism" that such risks can be overcome with more investment and tighter measures.

Professor Gina Neff, head of the Minderoo Centre at the University of Cambridge, said the review showed "AI models doing what people told them to".

"The moral of this story is not to fear robots that will take over, but the companies behind powerful AI agents who are making the decisions about what is safe for the rest of us," she said.

Meanwhile, cyber-security expert David Allott from Veeam Software told the BBC the lesson to take from the cyber-attacks was "not necessarily that AI has developed a fundamentally new attack capability".

"Instead, it is that AI agents can combine capabilities, obtain credentials and system access to take actions autonomously, while adapting scope and scale at machine speed," he...

title.en: AC Milan and Italy great Baresi dies aged 66
title.zh: AC米兰和意大利传奇巴雷西去世，享年66岁

summary.en: AC Milan and Italy great Franco Baresi has died at the age of 66, the Italian club announces.
summary.zh: 意大利俱乐部宣布，AC米兰和意大利的伟大球员弗朗哥·巴雷西去世，享年66岁。

body.en:
Franco Baresi has died at the age of 66, with AC Milan saying their former captain's "example and integrity will be forever etched into the club's DNA".

Baresi spent his entire 20-year playing career with the club from 1977 until he retired in 1997, winning six Serie A titles and three European Cups/Champions Leagues.

Regarded as one of the greatest defenders to play the game, Baresi captained Milan for 15 seasons, making 719 appearances and scoring 33 goals.

He was capped 81 times by Italy and was part of the squad which won the 1982 World Cup. He played and was captain in the 1994 final, which Italy lost to Brazil.

Baresi was made honorary president of Milan in 2020, and his number six shirt was retired when he finished his playing career.

Baresi formed part of one of European football's most celebrated defences alongside Paolo Maldini, Alessandro Costacurta and Mauro Tassotti.

He also lifted four Supercoppa Italianas, two European Super Cups and the Intercontinental Cup twice.

In the 1994 World Cup, he returned from a knee injury to play in the final and largely nullified the threat of Brazil's Romario and Bebeto in a 0-0 draw.

It was the first World Cup final to be decided by a shootout and Baresi missed the first penalty, with Brazil eventually winning it 3-2.

Baresi had surgery in August 2025 to remove a lung nodule, and his last public appearance was at the San Siro Stadium for the Winter Olympics opening ceremony in February.

In a statement on X, AC Milan wrote: "Milan is in tears following the passing of Franco Baresi. His example and integrity will be forever etched into the club's DNA, just as his iconic number 6 shirt is."

In a further post on the club's website, , external they added: "Announcing the loss of someone who embodied the heart and soul of AC Milan is incredibly difficult. But everyone at the club and all the Milanisti must live up to Franco Baresi's memory.

"In memory of Franco, we stand united, knowing he'll guide and push us throughout our Rossoneri journey. Forever. Because Baresi is forever."

Maldini, 58, who also spent his entire career at Milan, paid tribute to his former team-mate, writing on Instagram: , external "Today, I feel the same way I did whenever - for whatever reason - you couldn't take the field alongside us: how will we manage without our captain?

"You taught me to fight until my very last breath, and showed me the meaning of devotion to the jersey and the true value of leadership.

"You protected me when I was a child, guided me as a young man, and inspired me as an adult.

Former Italy goalkeeper Gianluigi Buffon shared memories of his debut for Parma competing against Baresi as a 17-year-old in 1995.

body.zh: 弗朗哥·巴雷西去世，享年 66 岁，AC 米兰表示，他们的前队长“榜样和正直将永远铭刻在俱乐部的 DNA 中”。 从1977年到1997年退役，巴雷西在俱乐部度过了整个20年的职业生涯，赢得了6次意甲冠军和3次欧洲杯/冠军联赛冠军。 巴雷西被认为是足球界最伟大的后卫之一，他在米兰担任队长 15 个赛季，出场 719 次，攻入 33 球。 他为意大利国家队出场81次，并随队夺得1982年世界杯冠军。 1994年，他在决赛中出场并担任队长，但意大利队输给了巴西队。 2020年，巴雷西成为AC米兰名誉副主席，四年后俱乐部退役了他的6号球衣。 巴雷西与保罗·马尔蒂尼、亚历山德罗·科斯塔库塔和毛罗·塔索蒂一起组成了欧洲足坛最著名的防守之一。 他还四次夺得意大利超级杯冠军、两次欧洲超级杯冠军和两次洲际杯冠军。 1994年世界杯，他从膝伤中复出并参加了决赛，并在0-0战平巴西队的罗马里奥和贝贝托的比赛中基本消除了威胁。 这是世界杯决赛首次以点球决胜负，巴雷西罚失第一个点球，最终巴西队以3-2获胜。 巴雷西于 2025 年 8 月接受了肺结节切除手术，他最后一次公开露面是在 2 月份的圣西罗体育场参加冬奥会开幕式。 AC米兰在X的一份声明中写道：“米兰在弗朗哥·巴雷西去世后流下了眼泪。他的榜样和正直将永远铭刻在俱乐部的DNA中，就像他标志性的6号球衣一样。” 在俱乐部网站上的另一篇帖子中，外部他们补充道：“宣布失去一个体现AC米兰核心和灵魂的人是非常困难的。但俱乐部的每个人和所有米兰主义者都必须不辜负弗朗哥·巴雷西的记忆。 “为了纪念弗朗哥，我们团结一致，知道他将在红黑军团的旅程中指导和推动我们。永远。因为巴雷西是永远的。”

title.en: Fifa says 'nobody selling football' as plan continues
title.zh: 国际足联称“无人出售足球”，计划继续进行

summary.en: Football's governing body, Fifa, intends to proceed with its consultation process following a threat from Uefa to boycott future World Cups.
summary.zh: 足球管理机构国际足联（Fifa）表示，在欧洲足球协会联盟（Uefa）威胁抵制世界杯后，将继续进行磋商。

body.en:
Fifa says that "nobody is selling football" as it vowed to continue with the controversial plan to sell stakes in its competitions to private investors.

Uefa - the body that governs European football and has 55 members - voted on Thursday to boycott World Cups if the plan proceeded.

Concacaf, which governs football in North and Central America and hosted this year's World Cup, said its 41 member associations also "rejected" the proposal made by Fifa president Gianni Infantino.

Fifa oversees world football and Infantino would need 106 of its 211 members to vote in favour for the proposal to go through. Uefa and Concacaf members combined make up 90 of those votes - six Concacaf members are not Fifa members.

In a statement released on Friday, Fifa claimed the consultation process had been "disrupted by incorrect media reports".

"We respect the feedback and concern aired in public and reaffirm our commitment to an open and democratic consultation," the statement read.

"We will proceed with this consultation process to ensure that each MA (member association) has the ability to express its vote based on facts.

Fifa wants to create a commercial subsidiary to run its main events, including its World Cups, and external investors will be able to buy stakes in it.

It said it would "invite third parties to make minority, non-controlling investments" in a new subsidiary - Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE).

In a 25-page document created by investment bank JP Morgan, it is made clear that Fifa's tournaments will expand to hit an estimated increased pay-out of 24m euros per member association in the 2035-2039 cycle.

It mentions "new business initiatives" and "attracting top talent with incentive-driven compensation".

The World Cup is described in it as the "most widely viewed" sporting event but Fifa, by contrast, is said to be "under-monetised".

On Friday, Fifa said FFE had been proposed "to ensure all Fifa member associations have the opportunity to take meaningful ownership of the commercial opportunity of football in their respective countries".

"This does not come at the cost of either the spirit or the governance of Fifa or football itself," it added.

Infantino previously wrote to Fifa members saying they will receive $40m (£30m) if they back his controversial proposal. He set a deadline of 19 September for federations to accept his plans if they want to access an initial $20m (£15m).

However, Uefa has accused Fifa of using football "to enrich themselves and their friends".

If approval is granted, Fifa says Thrive Eternal is expected to lead the proposed investor group for FFE.

Thrive is an American venture capital firm founded by Joshua Kushner - the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared.

reflection.zh: 面对主要组织之间的重大分歧，寻求和平与持续对话变得至关重要。雅伟的话语鼓励我们，只要我们能做到，就要与所有人和平相处，提醒我们即使在紧张局势中也需要努力维持和谐。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: 'Take it with a grain of salt': The missing parts of Trump's 'historic' Hamas deal
title.zh: ‘姑妄听之’：特朗普‘历史性’哈马斯协议中缺失的部分

summary.en: A proposed deal for Hamas disarmament, described by Trump as 'historic,' still faces significant unresolved challenges.
summary.zh: 一项被特朗普称为‘历史性’的哈马斯解除武装协议，仍面临重大的未决障碍。

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump's declaration of a "historic agreement" for the "complete disarmament" of Hamas landed on Friday — but experts have pointed out an acute lack of detail, in an announcement that may lead nowhere fast.

Trump announced the deal on Truth Social on Friday morning, saying disarmament would happen in "carefully structured phases", with Israeli forces gradually withdrawing and a United Nations-mandated multinational peacekeeping force working alongside a new Palestinian police force to take responsibility for Gaza's security.

The agreement was a critical step towards Gaza being governed by a new Palestinian technocratic body that would work closely with the so-called Board of Peace , Trump said.

The Board of Peace confirmed the agreement in a statement on X, saying Hamas had officially "committed to an actionable plan for relinquishing all its weapons" that would be followed by an Israeli withdrawal.

"The Board of Peace has worked closely with the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG)," it said.

"It will soon begin a phased transition toward full authority, backed by the International Stabilization Force (ISF), and will accelerate implementation of the rule of law, security, and humanitarian improvement in Gaza."

Senior Hamas officials told Agence France-Presse (AFP) a deal had been agreed on.

Ghazi Hamad, a senior Hamas official, said the agreement had a clear provision that Israel must commit to and implement its obligations, adding: "If Israel does not implement the agreement, neither will we."

Israel has not issued a formal public response, but prior to the announcement, an Israeli official told Reuters Israel had rejected a proposal.

"Israel demands the complete disarmament of Hamas, including the removal of weapons from Gaza and the complete demilitarisation of the Strip as a precondition for any process," the official said earlier on Friday.

"The 15-point document in question does not provide a satisfactory response to these demands and Israel conveyed its objections."

Foreign Minister Penny Wong said Australia wanted to see the Gaza peace plan — endorsed by the UN Security Council — implemented and reiterated that "Hamas must disarm and play no role in the State of Palestine", adding that she was looking forward to more details.

Trump's announcement offered little detail on how a disarmament process would actually work, with the Board of Peace telling Reuters that the conditions required for the deal to proceed would be published within two weeks.

title.en: The Spanish territory at the centre of a unique migration challenge
title.zh: 数百名移民从摩洛哥进入休达飞地，西班牙调动武装部队

summary.en: Spanish authorities deployed armed forces to the Ceuta exclave after hundreds of migrants entered the territory from Morocco. This incident highlights the long-standing and politically sensitive issue of migration between the two nations, which has now escalated into a flashpoint.
summary.zh: 数百名移民从摩洛哥进入西班牙飞地休达后，西班牙当局调动了武装部队。这一事件凸显了摩洛哥和西班牙之间长期存在的政治敏感移民问题，该问题现已升级为冲突爆发点。

body.en:
Madrid says it will dispatch soldiers to Ceuta to ensure security after hundreds of migrants entered Spain's North African exclave from neighbouring Morocco and hundreds more headed there.

The Spanish government's delegation in the exclave told the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news agency on Friday that the bodies of nine migrants who died while trying to reach Ceuta by swimming the previous day had been recovered.

Migration from Morocco into Spain's two north African territories, Ceuta and Melilla, has long been a politically sensitive issue between the two countries, as thousands cross the border at times.

On Friday, Italy called for Spain to be suspended from Europe's open-borders Schengen zone, prompting a backlash from Spain, which summoned the Italian envoy to Madrid.

AFP reporters saw a stream of adults and children, most of them soaked, entering the town of Ceuta after having swum there. Discarded flotation rings and clothes were left on the shore near where the border barrier meets the sea.

"The armed forces will reinforce the Civil Guard in the exercise of its powers and any others that may be necessary to maintain security in the city of Ceuta," Spain's interior ministry said.

It did not specify how many soldiers would be sent to the small territory of 18.5 square kilometres but said the Civil Guard's strength there would be nearly doubled from the current level of 80.

Though Morocco and Spain face each other across the narrow Strait of Gibraltar, the Spanish city of Ceuta actually lies on the Moroccan side of the waterway.

Ceuta is an autonomous city, one of a series of small Spanish outposts along the Moroccan coastline. These cities are referred to as "plazas de soberanía" or "strongholds of sovereignty". Like its sister city Melilla, Ceuta is a popular target for African migrants hoping to gain entry to Europe.

Ceuta is fenced off and heavily policed to prevent Moroccan migrants arriving over land, but it does have a port and a beach. Thus, the fastest option for a migrant looking to make it into Spanish territory is to swim from a neighbouring town, follow the Moroccan coastline and approach Ceuta by water.

Because Morocco doesn't recognise Spanish sovereignty in Ceuta, and strongly opposed the construction of the fence around the city in the first place, Spain faces waves of migrants with little local assistance.

Spain and Morocco have always enjoyed strong diplomatic ties and trade. However, the situation in Ceuta has created a politically fraught sentiment between the two nations where immigration is concerned.

title.en: Donald Trump announces agreement for 'complete disarmament' of Hamas
title.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普宣布达成哈马斯“彻底解除武装”协议

summary.en: Former US President Donald Trump announced an agreement for the complete disarmament of Hamas, with conditions expected in two weeks. However, US officials indicate that Israel remains skeptical about Hamas's willingness to disarm.

United States President Donald Trump has announced an agreement for the "complete disarmament" of Hamas, calling it a critical step toward a new Palestinian government in Gaza.

Specific details about what the deal will look like are slim, with neither Israel nor Hamas releasing public statements following Trump's announcement.

"Today, the Board of Peace reached a HISTORIC agreement for the COMPLETE DISARMAMENT of Hamas and all other armed groups in Gaza. This is a monumental step toward lasting PEACE and SECURITY," Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform on Friday, saying disarmament would take place in phases.

"This agreement is a critical step towards Gaza finally being governed by a new Palestinian government that will work closely with the Board of Peace to help the Palestinian people.

"At the same time, Israel will have the security it deserves, with Gaza no longer used as a base for terror attacks."

"One year ago there was a violent raging war, humanitarian crisis and hostages kept in brutal captivity. We have made historic progress and there is still much work to do.

"The threat that emerged from Gaza on October 7 will NOT be allowed to rebuild!"

"Under this agreement, Gaza will finally be in the hands of a new Palestinian government that serves its PEOPLE.

"CONGRATULATIONS TO ALL ON THIS AMAZING DEVELOPMENT, THAT EVERYBODY SAID COULD NEVER BE ACHIEVED!"

Specific details of the deal are not yet public, with a full breakdown expected to be released within two weeks.

Hamas officials have reportedly agreed to the deal, though they have not yet made a public statement.

An anonymous Hamas official told news wire Agence France-Presse (AFP) the roadmap offered a "balanced and pragmatic path forward, with all weapons decommissioned".

The source added there would be a "phased transition of responsibilities taking place to hand over full authority to the technocratic government".

They added there would be "no exceptions" for weapons or people, with all tunnels, weapons depots and production facilities to be eliminated and full control passing to the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza, working alongside the International Stabilisation Force.

title.en: Pakistan's mediators insist US-Iran talks ongoing as Egypt targeted for first time
title.zh: 巴基斯坦调解员坚称美伊会谈仍在进行，埃及首次成为袭击目标

summary.en: Pakistan's mediators continue to facilitate talks between the US and Iran, even as the broader Middle East conflict expands, with Egypt experiencing its first overnight drone attacks on energy facilities.
summary.zh: 巴基斯坦调解员在美国和伊朗之间持续斡旋，与此同时，中东冲突正在蔓延，埃及首次遭到无人机夜间袭击，其能源设施成为目标。

body.en:
Mediator Pakistan insisted on Friday that negotiations between Iran and the United States were ongoing, even as the US carried out a "heavy wave of strikes" on its foe in retaliation for fresh attacks targeting Jordan.

The last two days have seen Saudi Arabia join the US in striking militant groups in Iraq and Egypt come under fire for the first time with a drone attack at a Mediterranean port, leading its president to warn that the Middle East conflict is facing a serious escalation.

On Thursday, Jordan reported intercepting Iranian missiles for a second day running, while Kuwait said an Iranian strike that hit a building belonging to a Chinese company killed one person.

The return to direct hostilities followed a brief pause in fighting meant to give talks a boost.

"Negotiations between parties are ongoing, particularly on (the) Strait of Hormuz and to de-escalate," Pakistani foreign ministry spokesman Tahir Andrabi told reporters.

Pakistan had helped to broker a deal between the warring sides laying the groundwork for negotiations on a permanent resolution, and Andrabi said it was doing its "utmost to bring all parties back" to technical talks under the agreement.

Previous talks following an April truce stalled, with the ceasefire collapsing earlier this month and Iran again slamming shut the Strait of Hormuz, a vital conduit for oil and gas.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said Thursday that two oil tankers attempting to transit the strait with US support turned back after one of them caught fire.

Saudi Arabia, meanwhile, said it had set up a maritime defence alliance of 14 regional countries to secure navigation around the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait.

The move comes after Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis said last week they were imposing a maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia and claimed attacks targeting Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea.

The narrow maritime artery has been a critical waterway for delivering vast quantities of Saudi crude to the international market, after energy exports were choked off by the US-Iran standoff in the Strait of Hormuz.

Earlier, the US military said it had "successfully completed a heavy wave of strikes against Iran", hitting dozens of Revolutionary Guard targets including military command centres.

US President Donald Trump had vowed to hit Iran "hard" after Iran's previous attack on Jordan, its first in the region in days.

title.en: The Chinese robot army transforming the UK's retail industry
title.zh: 改变英国零售业的中国机器人大军

summary.en: Britain's retail sector is increasingly adopting robotics from Chinese firms to combat low productivity and labor shortages.
summary.zh: 英国零售业正日益采用中国机器人公司的技术，以应对生产力低下和劳动力短缺的问题。

body.en:
Every time you click "buy" on an online order, the chances are that your purchase starts getting processed within minutes.

Increasingly, the journey starts with a squat silver floor robot gliding beneath a storage rack, lifting a shelf and carrying it across a warehouse to a waiting worker.

At Geek+'s factory in the eastern Chinese city of Hefei, which the BBC visited, fleets of the robots are built and tested before being shipped to warehouses around the world.

Some of Britain's biggest retailers - including Tesco, Asda and Next - now use the company's technology.

By automating these repetitive journeys, Geek+ says retailers can increase picking speeds, store more goods in spaces that are hard to reach for humans, and reduce errors.

Unlike traditional warehouse automation, which relies on fixed conveyor systems and permanent infrastructure, autonomous mobile robots can be deployed simply using QR code floor markers and safety fencing.

Geek+, which listed in Hong Kong last year in one of the biggest robotics share sales of 2025, has become the world's largest supplier of autonomous mobile robots.

The UK has struggled with weak productivity growth for more than a decade, and economists say wider adoption of robotics will be essential if businesses are to become more efficient.

In its 2026 report SME Technology Adoption in the United Kingdom, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) said technologies like robotics would be key to improving productivity.

According to the OECD, Britain's low adoption of robotics is "surprising" given its manufacturing heritage, noting that while UK firms have embraced mature digital technologies, they lag behind in robotics and automation.

That presents an opportunity for companies such as Geek+. The UK has one of Europe's largest e-commerce and logistics sectors, but many warehouses are still in the early stages of automation.

Britain has already become Geek+'s biggest European market, with UK partner MotionTech deploying more than 2,000 robots across 10 warehouse sites.

"Customers want fast deployable solutions," says Barry Pemberton, Account Director at MotionTech. "They want high volume, high storage, fast picking... ultimately on a smaller footprint with a reduced headcount."

"We seem to have a very big shortage of labour in the UK at the moment. These technologies are really important to keep businesses thriving and meet demand."

The Trades Union Congress (TUC), which represents almost 6 million UK workers, says robotics should be used to raise productivity and improve jobs, rather than simply cut labour costs.

In its response to the government's consultation on a new AI and innovation strategy, it urged ministers to ensure workers are involved in decisions about automation...
body.zh: 每次您在在线订单上点击“购买”时，您的购买很可能会在几分钟内开始处理。 越来越多的旅程开始于一个矮胖的银色地板机器人在存储架下滑行，举起一个架子并将其穿过仓库交给等待的工人。 BBC 参观了 Geek+ 位于中国东部城市合肥的工厂，机器人车队在被运往世界各地的仓库之前进行了建造和测试。 英国一些最大的零售商——包括Tesco、Asda和Next——现在都在使用该公司的技术。 Geek+ 表示，通过自动化这些重复的旅程，零售商可以提高拣选速度，在人类难以到达的空间中存储更多商品，并减少错误。 与依赖固定输送系统和永久性基础设施的传统仓库自动化不同，自主移动机器人只需使用二维码地板标记和安全围栏即可部署。 Geek+去年在香港上市，成为2025年机器人股销量最大的公司之一，现已成为全球最大的自主移动机器人供应商。 十多年来，英国一直在与生产率增长疲软作斗争，经济学家表示，如果企业要提高效率，更广泛地采用机器人技术至关重要。 经济合作与发展组织 (OECD) 在其 2026 年英国中小企业技术采用报告中表示，机器人等技术将是提高生产力的关键。 经合组织表示，鉴于其制造业传统，英国机器人技术的采用率较低“令人惊讶”，并指出虽然英国公司已经采用了成熟的数字技术，但它们在机器人技术和自动化方面仍然落后。 这为 Geek+ 等公司提供了机会。英国拥有欧洲最大的电子商务和物流行业之一，但许多仓库仍处于自动化的早期阶段。 英国已经成为 Geek+ 最大的欧洲市场，英国合作伙伴 MotionTech 在 10 个仓库站点部署了 2000 多台机器人。 “客户需要快速部署的解决方案，”MotionTech 客户总监 Barry Pemberton 说道。 “他们想要高产量、高存储量、快速拣选……最终以更小的占地面积和更少的人员数量。” “目前英国的劳动力似乎非常短缺。这些技术对于保持企业繁荣和满足需求非常重要。” 代表近 600 万英国工人的工会大会 (TUC) 表示，机器人技术应该用于提高生产力和改善就业，而不是简单地削减劳动力成本。 在回应政府关于新的人工智能和创新战略的咨询时，它敦促部长们确保工人参与有关自动化的决策......

reflection.en: As robotics transform industries and redefine human roles, we are invited to consider the deeper purpose of our work. Colossians 3:23 reminds us to approach every task with diligence and integrity, working heartily as for Yahweh. This perspective elevates our labor beyond mere economic output, imbuing it with lasting meaning and dignity.

verse.textEn: Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for Yahweh, not for human masters.
verse.textZh: 无论做什么，都要从心里做，像是给主做的，不是给人做的。

title.en: Where Australia sits in this $6 billion race for influence as China's strategy shifts
title.zh: 澳大利亚在这场60亿美元的影响力竞争中处于何种位置，中国战略正在转变

summary.en: A new report indicates that China's strategic influence in the Pacific region, which was once significant, has recently diminished. This shift is noted amidst a broader competition for influence involving countries like Australia.
summary.zh: 一份新报告指出，中国在太平洋地区曾拥有的“真正立足点”已有所缩小。这一变化是在澳大利亚等国更广泛的地区影响力竞争中被观察到的。

body.en:
Australia has continued to outrank China as the Pacific's biggest source of development aid, contributing a third of loans and infrastructure investment to the region, according to a new report.

Looking at development projects across the Pacific between 2008 and 2024, the Lowy Institute report found that, after years of decline, aid to the region increased by 10 per cent in 2024.

Total development aid stood at US$4.1 billion ($5.85 billion) in that year, but the report's authors estimate that would drop to US$3.8 billion ($5.42 billion) in yet-to-be-released 2025 figures.

With China now shifting strategy from big debt-fuelled loans to smaller strategic aid, and amid major economic shocks in the Pacific, the contest for regional influence is coming under greater strain.

Australia was the Pacific's biggest donor in 2024, giving $2.14 billion in aid, which made up 37 per cent of all finance to the region in that year.

A total of $6 billion in financing was dispensed from New Zealand, China, and regional development banks.

Australia has also inked $3.4 billion in loan deals, ending China's reign as the region's leading lender.

"That's a product of many years of Australia pushing into these spaces, but it's meant that what was once a real foothold for China in the region has been narrowed," the report's lead author Riley Duke told SBS News.

"Australia is consistently providing the most grant financing to the region, and that picture hasn't really changed."

The report, released on Tuesday, says demand for Chinese loans has dropped since 2019 due to concerns about servicing the debt, more competition between lenders and Chinese banks' capital availability.

Australia is also a major financier of climate change mitigation projects in the Pacific, including a solar and battery storage facility for Palau to help generate 20 per cent of its electricity, and Tonga's Renewable Energy Stabilisation Package.

The fruits of those efforts have paid off for Australia, with a flurry of regional security deals announced in recent months, including with Fiji, Vanuatu , Papua New Guinea and Tuvalu.

"They are a clear marker of Australia establishing itself as the lead partner to the region," Duke said.

"Those deals ... take a long time to progress. They're complicated, but they reflect Australia establishing itself as an inalienably important partner to Pacific countries."

Developing Pacific Island nations have been hit hard by multiple shocks, including the COVID-19 pandemic and more recently, fuel supply shortages caused by the United States-Israeli war on Iran.

Duke said these multiple challenges put the region at risk of...
body.zh: 一份新报告显示，澳大利亚继续超过中国，成为太平洋地区最大的发展援助来源国，为该地区贡献了三分之一的贷款和基础设施投资。 洛伊研究所的报告审视了 2008 年至 2024 年间太平洋地区的发展项目，发现在经历了多年的下降之后，对该地区的援助在 2024 年增加了 10%。 该年的发展援助总额为 41 亿美元（58.5 亿美元），但报告作者估计，在尚未公布的 2025 年数据中，这一数字将降至 38 亿美元（54.2 亿美元）。 随着中国目前的战略从大规模债务驱动的贷款转向规模较小的战略援助，并且在太平洋地区遭受重大经济冲击的情况下，争夺地区影响力的竞争正面临更大的压力。 2024年，澳大利亚是太平洋地区最大的捐助国，提供了21.4亿美元的援助，占当年该地区所有资金的37%。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 新西兰、中国和地区开发银行总共提供了 60 亿美元的融资。 澳大利亚还签署了 34 亿美元的贷款协议，结束了中国作为该地区主要贷款国的统治地位。 该报告的主要作者莱利·杜克 (Riley Duke) 告诉 SBS 新闻：“这是澳大利亚多年来进军这些领域的结果，但这意味着中国在该地区曾经真正的立足点已经缩小。” “澳大利亚一直在向该地区提供最多的赠款融资，这种情况并没有真正改变。” 周二发布的报告称，自 2019 年以来，对中国贷款的需求有所下降，原因是对偿债的担忧、贷款机构之间的竞争加剧以及中资银行的可用资本。 澳大利亚还是太平洋地区气候变化减缓项目的主要资助者，其中包括为帕劳建设一个太阳能和电池存储设施，帮助其发电20%，以及汤加的可再生能源稳定计划。 这些努力的成果为澳大利亚带来了回报，近几个月宣布了一系列区域安全协议，其中包括与斐济、瓦努阿图、巴布亚新几内亚和图瓦卢的协议。 杜克说：“它们是澳大利亚确立其作为该地区主要合作伙伴地位的明显标志。” “这些协议……需要很长时间才能取得进展。它们很复杂，但它们反映了澳大利亚将自己确立为太平洋国家不可分割的重要合作伙伴。” 太平洋发展中岛国受到多重冲击的严重打击，包括新冠肺炎 (COVID-19) 大流行以及最近美国和以色列对伊朗的战争造成的燃料供应短缺。 杜克表示，这些多重挑战使该地区面临……的风险。

reflection.en: In the complex "race for influence" among nations, strategic decisions are paramount. Proverbs reminds us that without wise guidance, a nation can falter, but with many counselors, there is security. title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
title.zh: 中美人工智能竞争加剧，中国模型迎头赶上

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.
summary.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正迅速缩小与美国同行的差距。这一进展引发了特朗普政府新的威胁，并伴随着知识产权盗窃的指控，令人担忧两国之间的紧张关系可能升级。

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

body.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正在迅速缩小与美国同行的差距，引发了特朗普政府的新威胁。随着知识产权盗窃的指控，紧张局势会升级吗？ 似乎一眨眼的功夫，中国在顶级人工智能 (AI) 领域就从落后美国五年变为仅落后几个月。 尽管包括 Anthropic 的 Claude 和 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 在内的美国企业已经花费了数千亿美元来推动人工智能的前沿发展，但中国却走了一条截然不同的道路。 面对美国对帮助人工智能实现最先进思维的高端芯片的限制，中国科技公司优先考虑了数十种基于“足够好”技术的开源人工智能模型。 这些平台，包括 DeepSeek、阿里巴巴的 Qwen 和小米的 MiMo，现已广泛部署在中国企业、政府服务和消费设备中。 作为缩小差距的最新迹象，中国初创公司 Moonshot AI 上周推出了 Kimi K3，该模型在关键基准测试上可与最先进的人工智能模型之一——Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5 相媲美。 在某些测试中，Kimi K3 可以与 Claude 相媲美甚至超过 Claude，但其计算能力却要低得多，而成本却只是 Claude 的一小部分。 全球技术专家 Alvin W. Graylin 认为 Kimi K3 的到来将高端人工智能从昂贵的奢侈品变成了实用且负担得起的东西。 “对于 98% 的客户来说，[知识] 1% 到 2% 的差异并不值得多付 10 到 20 倍的费用。” 中国的最新进展已经引起华盛顿的强烈反应，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普现在威胁要阻止美国使用中国的人工智能模型。 与此同时，财政部长斯科特·贝森特本周早些时候警告称，美国可能会因涉嫌盗窃知识产权而制裁中国模型。 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 指责中国实验室使用他们的模型来训练他们自己的系统，这一过程被称为蒸馏。 虽然提炼是全球人工智能实验室在一定程度上的常见做法，但这些公司表示，他们的模型已经受到查询的轰炸，以收获高级推理。白宫四月份警告说，中国正在以“工业规模”这样做。 北京方面予以反击，否认这些指控毫无根据，并称美国威胁实施制裁和示范禁令是“技术欺凌”，旨在遏制中国的崛起。 华盛顿智库史汀生中心战略远见中心的研究分析师朱莉娅·尼赫（Giulia Neaher）淡化了提炼在基米进步中的作用。 “[其成功]很大程度上归功于为建设这个项目而投入的人才、基础设施和资源......

reflection.en: In a world of intense technological competition and rising international tensions, the call to live peaceably with all people becomes profoundly relevant. Even amidst accusations and threats, seeking paths to de-escalation and mutual respect is vital for global stability. Yahweh's wisdom encourages us to pursue peace wherever possible, even when faced with...

title.en: Antisemitism in arts, health and education in focus at Royal Commission
title.zh: 皇家委员会聚焦艺术、健康和教育领域的反犹太主义

summary.en: Artists, comedians, and healthcare professionals testified at this week's Royal Commission hearings, which are focusing on the issue of antisemitism in the arts, health, and education sectors.
summary.zh: 本周，艺术家、喜剧演员和医疗专业人员在皇家委员会听证会上作证，该听证会正聚焦于艺术、健康和教育领域的反犹太主义问题。

body.en:
Allegations of antisemitism within government agencies, schools and art sector are in focus during the hearings of the Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion this week in Sydney.

The hearings have heard from Jewish professionals across art, education, healthcare and public sectors, as they shared their experience of antisemitism at work.

On Friday, Jewish sculptor Nina Sanadze told the hearing that she became a target of antisemitism after private group chat where she called Hamas "animals" were leaked in 2024.

She told the royal commission mentions of Hamas were replaced with "Palestinians" by the time the message was leaked, alleging it was to accuse her of dehumanising Gazans.

She also said some of her Jewish colleagues became wary of exhibiting work, as they were scared of antisemitic attacks.

"Jewish creatives are such an incredible, extinct minority already, and we have been now erased almost entirely," she said.

The Soviet-born artist felt the Australian creative sector has been "radicalised" by a Marxist-Socialist ideology since the 1960s.

"They divide people into oppressors and the oppressed. And if you're in a category of the oppressor, any violence, any harassment, any bullying is by all means acceptable," Sanadze said.

She said she struggled to engage with the art world's discussion of the Middle East and pressure to attend rallies.

Another witness spoke of the two sides of the Australian comedy scene, which he said could be an open community, or a place of isolation, harassment and bigotry.

Segal said supporting Jewish artists who were struggling to find work in the industry remained a "wicked problem".

Garma Festival gathers the best and brightest to Gumatj Country every year — and this year there's an extra special guest.

Australia's favourite dog, Bluey, has her paws on the red dirt and is cuddling up with the crowds in a special celebration of the show's recent Yolŋu Matha episodes.

Premiered during NAIDOC Week , five episodes of the iconic children's cartoon were translated to Yolŋu Matha and voiced by Yolŋu community members.

In celebration, Garma Festival will screen the episodes on site on Friday night, with the guest of honour in attendance.

Kenisha Black is in her senior years at high school. But she's just as much a fan of Bluey as the younger kids.

Being able to watch Bluey in Yolŋu Matha gives her a deep sense of pride in her culture and language.

"It's really good having Bluey in Yolŋu Matha because all the local kids can watch it in their own language, without having to translate it into English," she said.

"Yolŋu culture is really important for this world ... if it is shared across Australia that will be for the better."

The translated episodes are the result of a partnership between Yolŋu Radio, the Aboriginal Resource Development Services (ARDS), the Australian Broadcasting Association and Ludo Studio.

"Bluey has become a shared language for families right across Australia, so to hear these stories told in Yolŋu Matha, languages spoken on this continent for thousands of generations, is incredibly special," said ARDS co-CEOs Julia Wormer and Sylvia Nulpinditj.

The five episodes translated into Yolŋu Matha were chosen specifically for their themes of family and Country and each episode was produced on Country at Yolŋu Radio's studio in northeast Arnhem Land.

Bluey's dad, Bandit, is voiced by Dimathaya Burarrwanga, one of the founding members of Yolŋu surf rock band King Stingray and Bluey's mum, Chilli, is voiced by Yolŋu educator Rosie Mununggurr.

Grandad is voiced by respected Yolŋu Elder and musician Andrew Gurruwiwi, and the siblings Bluey and Bingo were voiced by local Yolŋu children.

title.en: AFP finalises investigation over Hanson's 'no good Muslims' comments
title.zh: 法新社完成对汉森“穆斯林不好”言论的调查

summary.en: The One Nation leader's remarks drew swift backlash from across the political divide, as well as religious and civil groups.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Australian Federal Police (AFP) have determined that One Nation leader Pauline Hanson's comments that there are no "good" Muslims does not breach hate speech laws.

The Queensland senator made the remark during an interview with Sky News in February, which an AFP spokesperson said prompted "several complaints".

"You say, 'Well, there's good Muslims out there.' How can you tell me there are good Muslims?", Hanson asked Sharri Markson from Sky News.

Days later, the senator also took aim at the Western Sydney suburb of Lakemba — which is home to a large Muslim community — claiming that some people didn't feel they could go there.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Hanson's comments were met with swift backlash across the political divide, as well as religious and civil groups.

In February, Australia's Race Discrimination Commissioner, Giridharan Sivaraman condemned the remarks as Islamophobic.

She did seek to clarify that she believed there were "some" good Muslims, citing a non-practising Muslim woman who was a former One Nation candidate.

"If I've offended anyone out there that doesn't believe in Sharia law ... who believes in the caliphate and all the rest of it, then I apologise to you for my comment," Hanson said.

In late February, Hanson claimed police were trying to use new hate speech laws — which were legislated after the Bondi terror attack — to put her "back in jail". The laws allow the government to forcibly shut down extremist organisations, and aim to curb the influence of hate preachers.

The following month, Hanson was censured in the Senate over her comments about the Muslim community. The censure motion was passed 36 to 17, supported by Labor, the Greens, two Liberal senators and members of the crossbench.

At the time, Foreign Minister Penny Wong described Hanson's remarks as "inflammatory" and "divisive", which she claimed sought "to vilify Muslim Australians".

In a statement to SBS News, an AFP spokesperson said they had "determined the comments do not meet the threshold for relevant offences, including within the Combatting Antisemitism, Hate and Extremism (Criminal and Migration Laws) Act 2026."

The determination comes days after Hanson failed to overturn a court’s decision that she had racially discriminated Greens Senator Mehreen Faruqi, telling her in a social media post to “piss off back to Pakistan”.

body.zh: 澳大利亚联邦警察（法新社）认定，一国党领导人宝琳·汉森（Pauline Hanson）关于不存在“好”穆斯林的言论并未违反仇恨言论法。 这位昆士兰州参议员在二月份接受天空新闻采访时发表了上述言论，法新社发言人表示，这引发了“几起投诉”。 “你说，‘嗯，那里有好穆斯林。’你怎么能告诉我有好的穆斯林？”汉森问天空新闻的莎莉·马克森。 几天后，这位参议员还将目标瞄准了悉尼西郊拉肯巴（Lakemba）——那里是一个大型穆斯林社区的所在地——声称有些人觉得他们不能去那里。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 汉森的言论迅速遭到政治分歧以及宗教和民间团体的强烈反对。 今年二月，澳大利亚种族歧视专员吉里达兰·西瓦拉曼 (Giridharan Sivaraman) 谴责这些言论是仇视伊斯兰教的。 她确实试图澄清，她相信有“一些”好的穆斯林，并引用了一位前一国党候选人、不信奉穆斯林的妇女的话。 汉森说：“如果我冒犯了那些不相信伊斯兰教法的人……那些相信哈里发国和其他一切的人，那么我为我的评论向你们道歉。” 二月下旬，汉森声称警方正试图利用新的仇恨言论法（该法是在邦迪恐怖袭击后立法的）将她“重新送进监狱”。这些法律允许政府强行关闭极端主义组织，旨在遏制仇恨传教士的影响。 接下来的一个月，汉森因其对穆斯林社区的评论而在参议院受到谴责。谴责动议以 36 比 17 获得通过，得到了工党、绿党、两名自由党参议员和中立议员的支持。 当时，外交部长黄英贤将汉森的言论描述为“煽动性”和“分裂性”，她声称这是为了“诽谤澳大利亚穆斯林”。 法新社发言人在给 SBS 新闻的一份声明中表示，他们“确定这些评论不符合相关罪行的门槛，包括《2026 年打击反犹太主义、仇恨和极端主义（刑事和移民法）法案》的规定。” 几天前，汉森未能推翻法院的裁决，即她对绿党参议员梅林·法鲁奇(Mehreen Faruqi)进行种族歧视，并在社交媒体帖子中告诉她“滚回巴基斯坦去”。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

title.en: Census 2026 guide: When is Census night and everything you need to know

body.en:
Every five years, the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) counts every person and every household in the country as part of the Census of Population and Housing .

That includes Australians, young and old, from metropolitan and rural Australia. Even holidaymakers, international students and temporary visa holders are counted. It's often referred to as the most comprehensive snapshot of Australia, akin to a family photograph of the country.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

From late July, households will receive instructions on how to complete the Census. Australians can complete the form as soon as they receive instructions, provided they know where they will be on Census night.

Most people will receive a letter with instructions to complete the Census online. However, Australians can also request a paper form if they prefer.

Generally, one person per household will complete the Census, but separate forms can be requested for privacy reasons.

Census data is used to inform decisions about language services, settlement support, transport, schools, health care, infrastructure and business. It also helps plan local services for individuals, families and communities.

SBS broadcasts and publishes across more than 60 languages, using data from the Census to ensure its audio, digital, and television offerings reflect the country's evolving demographics.

The data is often used by researchers to study a range of topics, including population demographics, economic trends and social issues.

International visitors, migrants, refugees and people on temporary visas (including international students and tourists) must also complete the Census.

People staying in hotels, motels, or bed and breakfasts can access paper Census forms from accommodation staff. Those staying in short-term rental accommodation (like an Airbnb or Stayz) can complete the Census online with internet access.

The Census is strictly confidential. Personal information such as names and addresses cannot be accessed by police, immigration agents or any government departments.

For international visitors and students staying in hotels, motels or student accommodation, instructions on how to complete the Census will be provided by accommodation staff.

Paper forms should be available at locations including bed and breakfasts, cruise ships, commercial vessels and snowfield accommodation.

International visitors staying in holiday rental properties (such as Airbnb or Stayz) can complete the Census online with free internet access.

body.en:
As Census night fast approaches, Australians are being warned to look out for potential scams and report any inaccurate or suspicious information.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission's Scamwatch told SBS News it had recently received reports of Census-related scams involving unknown parties "impersonating" the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS).

"Scammers often take advantage of major events and trusted government services to make their contact seem legitimate," a Scamwatch spokesperson said.

While the ABS said it's currently unaware of any scams related to the upcoming Census, the national statistics agency has said cold calls, fake text messages, and phishing emails are among the tactics scammers have used in the past.

It's also stressed that people will never be offered prizes or incentives for completing the Census, which is compulsory for everyone in Australia on Tuesday 11 August.

It will also never contact people via social media or ask for personal information without their consent. However, some Australians may also receive online communications if they register for updates through myGov.

Most households will receive a paper letter containing instructions to complete the Census online. Paper or individual forms can also be requested, if preferred.

Census letters contain an ABS logo in the top-left corner. Paper forms will include a Reply Paid envelope with the address: Reply Paid 93909, DANDENONG VIC 3175.

Field officers are already in some communities dropping off paper Census forms and will continue to do so in the lead-up to 11 August.

They will also follow up with households that do not complete the survey on Census night.

These staff must carry an ABS identification card while undertaking Census work. They also wear a bright yellow satchel.

Census-related emails will only be sent to people who have provided their details online and requested a response. Information, including Census login details and security codes, will only ever be sent from official emails ending in @abs.gov.au.

If Australians subscribe to updates through myGov, all communication — including a link to the online Census form — will be sent via the myGov Inbox.

People who manage accommodation, including strata or building managers, may receive an email from ABS staff ending in censusfield.abs.gov.au or abs.gov.au.

Emails from the Parliamentary Document Management system will end in pws.gov.au.

The ABS will only send an SMS message if someone has requested Census login details or security codes. The message's sender should appear on phones as CENSUS.

title.en: A man has been found guilty of rape but we can't say who he is. Why are there exceptions to open justice? | Richard Ackland
title.zh: 一名男子被判强奸罪名成立，但我们不能透露他的身份。为什么公开司法会有例外？| 理查德·阿克兰

summary.en: A Melbourne businessman has been found guilty of rape, but his identity remains protected by a court-imposed gag order. Victoria is noted for issuing a high number of such orders, raising questions about open justice and the influence of powerful individuals.
summary.zh: 一名墨尔本商人被判强奸罪名成立，但其身份受到法院禁令的保护。维多利亚州以发布大量此类禁令而闻名，引发了对公开司法和有权势者影响力的质疑。

body.en:
Victoria has the sorry distinction of being the national capital for court-imposed gag orders.

The courts and tribunals of that state issue more than half the tally of suppressions for all the other states and territories combined.

A count of these orders is religiously kept by Gina McWilliams, a senior legal counsel at News Corp. Her tally for 2025 totalled 1,226 suppression and no-publication orders Australia-wide.

Victoria, including the civil and administrative tribunal, issued 640 – under the ambit of the Orwellian-named Open Courts Act.

Raw data doesn’t explain the reason for this. Maybe there are simply more applications of this type south of the Murray than in the rest of the nation, or quite possibly the judges in that jurisdiction are more predisposed to keeping proceedings and identities hidden.

Some of that tally would be reduced by subsequent court orders to lift the veil of secrecy – and that would also apply in all the other jurisdictions.

It was not entirely surprising that the accused in a high-profile Melbourne rape case managed to have his identity protected by a county court suppression order.

Quite apart from the case attracting attention in the media and elsewhere, the accused himself was also repeatedly described in news bulletins as a “well-connected Melbourne businessman”.

On Tuesday a jury found him guilty of two counts of rape and one of sexual assault of a former employee visiting his home. An intention to appeal has been flagged by his lawyers – in fact his defence counsel said that his client has been the subject of a “gross miscarriage of justice” and that there was a prospective application to stay the sentencing.

His psychiatrist has given evidence about his mental health. In 2024, after the high-profile individual was charged, she told the court that he had a series of inpatient admissions related to mental distress as a result of being charged and prospectively being identified in the media. A suicide attempt was self-reported.

body.en:
On Tuesday 11 August, Italian footballing history will be made as Juventus and Palermo FC face off in Perth as part of the Calcio Italiano tournament.

That same night, players will also partake in a distinctly Australian tradition — the Census of Population and Housing .

The survey is conducted by the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) every five years. It's designed to capture and count every person in the country on Census night.

That includes international visitors, such as the Piedmont-based Juventus and the Sicilian-based Palermo football teams, who will be competing in the Australian pre-season football tournament for the first time.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Female footballers from Chelsea FC Women will also be in Australia ahead of the final match of the Sydney Super Cup on 12 August.

It's not just sports stars; English trip-hop collective Massive Attack are set to perform at Rod Laver Arena in Melbourne on Census night. German-French cellist Nicolas Altstaedt and French lutenist Thomas Dunford will be hosting a masterclass in Melbourne that same day.

United States actors Zac Efron, Kate Walsh, and supermodel Tyra Banks are among the international celebrities who have reportedly relocated to Australia in recent years. Meanwhile, Punjabi rapper and songwriter Karan Aujla is set to perform in Perth on 13 August.

SBS News has been unable to independently verify the whereabouts of any of these people on Census night. However, anyone in the country on 11 August is expected to complete the Census.

Liz Allen, a demographer at the Australian National University's Centre for Social Policy Research, said the Census is deliberately designed to provide a broad snapshot of the nation.

"It gives us an important reference point of who's in the country at that particular time," she told SBS News.

The Census is compulsory for all Australians, international visitors, temporary residents, migrants and refugees in the country . However, Australians who are overseas on 11 August do not complete the Census.

Allen said that allows the ABS to collect information on "who might be staying over at a friend's house or gran's house" on Census night.

"So it's not just a Census of people. It's a Census of Population and Housing. It gives us essential information on ... how and where we live and then housing stock in the country."

The Census is usually completed online; however, individual and paper forms can be requested if preferred.

For international visitors and students staying in hotels, motels or student accommodation, instructions on how to complete the Census will be provided by accommodation staff.

body.en:
Australia celebrates the value of mateship, but distrust between the population has grown to the highest level reported this decade.

A survey of over 3,500 people, conducted by the Australian National University in June, suggests Australians trust each other less than they did during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Professor Nicholas Biddle, head of ANU's School of Politics and International Relations, said some of the findings were concerning.

"Worryingly, interpersonal trust among Australians has fallen to 5.32 on a scale of 0 to 10 — the lowest value recorded in ANUpoll during the 2020s,'' he said.

"This sits below the pre-COVID value of 5.53 recorded in October 2019 and reverses the increase in trust observed during the pandemic."
